cases.sentence: Уже смеркалось, когда князь Андрей и Пьер подъехали к ___ Лысогорского дома.
cases.explain: «главному подъезду» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: It was getting dusk when Prince Andréy and Pierre drove up to the front entrance of the house at Bald Hills. As they approached the house, Prince Andréy with a smile drew Pierre’s attention to a commotion going on at the back porch. A woman, bent with age, with a wallet on her back, and a short, long-haired, young man in a black garment had rushed back to the gate on seeing the carriage driving up. Two women ran out after them, and all four, looking round at the carriage, ran in dismay up the steps of the back porch.

cases.sentence: В то время как они подъезжали, князь Андрей с улыбкой обратил внимание Пьера на суматоху, происшедшую у ___.
cases.explain: «заднего крыльца» — after the preposition «у», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: It was getting dusk when Prince Andréy and Pierre drove up to the front entrance of the house at Bald Hills. As they approached the house, Prince Andréy with a smile drew Pierre’s attention to a commotion going on at the back porch. A woman, bent with age, with a wallet on her back, and a short, long-haired, young man in a black garment had rushed back to the gate on seeing the carriage driving up. Two women ran out after them, and all four, looking round at the carriage, ran in dismay up the steps of the back porch.

cases.sentence: Согнутая старушка с котомкой на спине, и ___ в черном одеянии и с длинными волосами, увидав въезжавшую коляску, бросились бежать назад в ворота.
cases.explain: «невысокий мужчина» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: It was getting dusk when Prince Andréy and Pierre drove up to the front entrance of the house at Bald Hills. As they approached the house, Prince Andréy with a smile drew Pierre’s attention to a commotion going on at the back porch. A woman, bent with age, with a wallet on her back, and a short, long-haired, young man in a black garment had rushed back to the gate on seeing the carriage driving up. Two women ran out after them, and all four, looking round at the carriage, ran in dismay up the steps of the back porch.

cases.explain: «божьи люди» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Those are Másha’s ‘God’s folk,’ ” said Prince Andréy. “They have mistaken us for my father. This is the one matter in which she disobeys him. He orders these pilgrims to be driven away, but she receives them.”

cases.explain: «божьи люди» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: Князь Андрей провел Пьера на свою половину, всегда в ___ ожидавшую его в доме его отца, и сам пошел в детскую.
cases.explain: «полной исправности» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Prince Andréy led Pierre to his own apartments, which were always kept in perfect order and readiness for him in his father’s house; he himself went to the nursery.

cases.sentence: — Пойдем к сестре, — сказал князь Андрей, возвратившись к Пьеру; — я еще не видал ее, она теперь прячется и сидит с своими ___.
cases.explain: «божьими людьми» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Let us go and see my sister,” he said to Pierre when he returned. “I have not found her yet, she is hiding now, sitting with her ‘God’s folk.’ It will serve her right, she will be confused, but you will see her ‘God’s folk.’ It’s really very curious.”

cases.sentence: Поделом ей, она сконфузится, а ты увидишь ___. C’est curieux, ma parole.[452] Это интересно, право.
cases.explain: «божьих людей» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Let us go and see my sister,” he said to Pierre when he returned. “I have not found her yet, she is hiding now, sitting with her ‘God’s folk.’ It will serve her right, she will be confused, but you will see her ‘God’s folk.’ It’s really very curious.”

cases.sentence: В ее ___ с лампадами перед киотами, на диване, за самоваром сидел рядом с ней молодой мальчик с длинным носом и длинными волосами и в монашеской рясе.
cases.explain: «уютной комнате» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Princess Márya really was disconcerted and red patches came on her face when they went in. In her snug room, with lamps burning before the icon stand, a young lad with a long nose and long hair, wearing a monk’s cassock, sat on the sofa beside her, behind a samovar. Near them, in an armchair, sat a thin, shriveled, old woman, with a meek expression on her childlike face.

cases.explain: «первыми фразами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Charmée de vous voir. Je suis très contente de vous voir,”53 she said to Pierre as he kissed her hand. She had known him as a child, and now his friendship with Andréy, his misfortune with his wife, and above all his kindly, simple face disposed her favorably toward him. She looked at him with her beautiful radiant eyes and seemed to say, “I like you very much, but please don’t laugh at my people.” After exchanging the first greetings, they sat down. “Ah, and Ivánushka is here too!” said Prince Andréy, glancing with a smile at the young pilgrim.
